facts.text: Nekoosa is known as the birthplace of Wood County, where Daniel Whitney built the first sawmill on the Wisconsin River in 1831.
The name Nekoosa comes from a Ho-Chunk word meaning running water, describing the river's five sets of rapids across three miles.
Historic Point Basse in Nekoosa is a living history museum featuring original nineteenth-century buildings like a one-room schoolhouse and blacksmith shop.
Nekoosa developed around the paper industry after the Nekoosa Paper Company established a mill there in 1893.
The settlement of Point Basse became a key hub for lumber raftsmen traveling from northern pineries to markets on the Mississippi River.
The Charles and JoAnn Lester Library is a notable local landmark that provides extensive resources for the Nekoosa community.
